summary: Controlled operational summary for community events: tickets, passes, check-in, multi-track schedule, CFP, accessibility, and registration states.
whenToUse: To present event operational information and actions to attendees and organizers in a single view.
whenNotToUse: To process payments, perform scans, or send requests to the server.
To create QR codes or certificates: the content is provided by the consumer.
For an event gallery: use EventCard.

props.name: now
props.description: Explicit reference instant for deterministic countdowns; the pattern does not update a timer.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone used to format times.

props.name: registrationDeadline
props.description: ISO registration deadline and its countdown.

props.name: tickets
props.description: Tiers, availability, controlled quantities, and registration/waitlist callbacks.

props.name: pass
props.description: Pass status and consumer-provided QR ReactNode content.

props.name: checkIn
props.description: Manual check-in status, details, and onCheckIn callback.

props.name: tracks
props.description: Sessions ordered by track; dates and data are provided by the consumer.

props.name: cfp
props.description: Proposal status, deadline, submission link or callback, and scorecard with reviewer feedback.

props.name: cancellation
props.description: Cancellation and refund status already determined by the consumer.

props.name: calendarHref / certificateHref
props.description: External links to export the calendar and view the certificate.

inherits: HTML attributes of section, including className.

keyboard.action: Reaches quantity controls, buttons, and links in reading order.
NumberInput handles quantities according to its own accessible behavior.
Activates a focused action or link.

accessibility: Sections are identified by headings; the schedule uses Agenda and its semantic lists.
Availability and states are described in text as well as by color.
Quantities are NumberInput fields with a tier-specific label.
QR and action results are consumer-supplied data; the pattern does not access the camera or server.
responsive: Panels are laid out in an adaptive grid; tiers, actions, and tracks wrap in narrow containers.
customization: Icons, Badge, Button, Link, NumberInput, and Agenda reuse design system primitives.
Internal styles are based exclusively on --dc-* tokens.
commonMistakes: Expecting quantities or states to persist: update the data in the consumer via callbacks.
Passing QR content generated here: the pass only accepts a ReactNode already created by the consumer.
Expecting live countdowns: provide a new now value externally if the time reference needs updating.
Using callbacks for payments, scans, or certificate generation: they are intentionally out of scope.

examples.name: AttendeeOperations
examples.title: Attendee operational details
examples.description: Selectable tiers, waitlist, pass, accessibility, links, and countdowns based on fixed instants.

examples.name: OrganizerOperations
examples.title: Organizer view
examples.description: Manual check-in, CFP status, refunds, and multi-track schedule.

limits: Does not perform server calls, payments, scanning/camera, raffles, or QR/certificate generation.
Countdowns and states do not update on their own: they are controlled by the consumer.
Ordering of tracks and sessions is left to the consumer.
